gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Plugable's own Intel-certified Thunderbolt 5 1 m cable (TBT5-240W1M, 80Gbps, 240W) sells for $34.95 on plugable.com today, the same price as the Thunderbolt 4 240W cable ChatGPT showed at $34.95. A shopper can get double the bandwidth with the same 240W rating for no extra money.
standout_why: Of the 17 results ChatGPT got, every product page and datasheet is USB4 or Thunderbolt 4 at 40Gbps: Plugable usb4-240w-1m (cited), tbt4-240w-1m (cited) and usbc-240w-1m, the StarTech 50c and 1m USB4 datasheets, ACT AC7451, Epico, Mouser/StarTech, Club 3D, and the Plugable USB4 resellers (Staples, CDW, B&H, Best Buy, device.report). None of them mentions a Thunderbolt 5 cable or its price. The plugable.com store text for tbt4-240w-1m describes only '40Gbps … 240W 48V/5A EPR'. Caveat: plugable.com returned HTTP 429 when I tried to open the two cited pages directly, so I compared against their titles and Plugable's own store-search text for the same URLs.
decides: This changes the pick. ChatGPT's 'best if you want Thunderbolt certification' card was Plugable TBT4-240W-1M at $34.95. Plugable's TBT5-240W1M costs the same $34.95 at plugable.com and is Intel-certified, 80Gbps and 240W, so it dominates the TB4 card. The 80 cm right-angle version of the same cable is explicitly 'fully backward compatible with Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 3, and USB4'. A second finding changes ChatGPT's 'longer cable' advice: a 40Gbps cable at 2 m is active, and Plugable's own 2 m Thunderbolt 4 cable is only 100W at $69.95. A long cable has to state 240W explicitly, as the Cable Matters 6.6 ft active Thunderbolt 4 cable does.
